module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Green's Open Problem 28

References:
- [Green, Ben. "100 open problems." (2024).](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.28)
- [Mathoverflow/339137](https://mathoverflow.net/questions/339137/why-do-polynomials-with-coefficients-0-1-like-to-have-only-factors-with-0-1) asked by user [Sil](https://mathoverflow.net/users/136794/sil)
- [MathStackexchange/3325163](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/3325163/) asked by user [Emmanuel Amiot](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/403309/emmanuel-amiot)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Green28

/-- True if a PMF on $\mathbb{Z}$ is uniformly distributed on its support. -/
def IsUniformOnSupport (X : PMF ℤ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (s : Finset ℤ) (hs : s.Nonempty), X = PMF.uniformOfFinset s hs

/--
The discrete convolution of two PMFs on $\mathbb{Z}$, representing the distribution of the sum of
two independent random variables.
-/
noncomputable def indepSum (X Y : PMF ℤ) : PMF ℤ := do
  let x ← X
  let y ← Y
  PMF.pure (x + y)

/--
Suppose that $X, Y$ are two finitely-supported independent random variables taking integer values,
and such that $X + Y$ is uniformly distributed on its range. Are $X$ and $Y$ themselves uniformly
distributed on their ranges?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 60]
theorem green_28 : answer(sorry) ↔
  ∀ (X Y : PMF ℤ), -- marginals, independence is built into indepSum
    X.support.Finite ∧ Y.support.Finite ∧ IsUniformOnSupport (indepSum X Y) →
      IsUniformOnSupport X ∧ IsUniformOnSupport Y := by
  sorry

end Green28

reformulations.difference: The source quantifies over independent integer-valued random variables; Lean instead quantifies over their marginal PMFs and uses indepSum, without an explicit probability space or independence hypothesis.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For independent variables with marginal PMFs p and q, the sum has mass ∑ₓ p(x)q(z−x) at z, exactly the formula for indepSum proved in the scratch file. Conversely, every pair of finitely supported PMFs can be realized as independent coordinate variables on the product of their supports, assigning probability p(x)q(y) to (x,y). Finite support and uniformity depend only on these laws. Moreover, PMF.support_uniformOfFinset ensures that the existential finset in IsUniformOnSupport is exactly the PMF's support. Thus the two formulations ask the same question; independence has not been omitted.

review.notes: Checked all three declarations. No mathematical defect or stale status was found; the consulted sources report only partial progress. /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles successfully and proves the convolution and support formulas, equivalence of IsUniformOnSupport with equal masses on a finite support, and singleton boundary cases. Exact tests show that uniforms on {0,1} and {0,2} have uniform sum on {0,1,2,3}, whereas summing two uniforms on {0,1} is not uniform. These checks establish that the hypothesis is satisfiable and the uniformity predicate is nontrivial. The full random-variable/PMF equivalence is justified mathematically above, rather than proved in Lean. The reviewed file was not modified.
